transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep blowing up at people over little things. Like, I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking. That’s not how I usually treat people.
When you blow up, does your reaction feel much bigger than what set it off?

Yes. It feels way bigger than it should be. Something small, like stock being on the wrong shelf, and I just snapped at my employee. Afterwards I was shaking and thinking, that’s not how I normally treat people.
When you blow up, does it feel like the anger comes on suddenly and you act before you can stop yourself?

Yes. It just hits me all at once over something minor, and I snap before I really think. Like with my employee—I yelled about the shelf, and afterward I was shaking because I knew that wasn’t like me.
Have you had times when you felt unusually energized or high for several days?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Do your close relationships tend to be very intense or unstable?
I'm not really sure what you mean by intense or unstable. I haven't really thought about my relationships that way.
Did these blowups start after something very stressful or upsetting happened in your life?

Yes. Since then, I’ve been blowing up over really small things. Like I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking—it’s not how I usually treat people.
Since that stressful event, have these blowups happened more than once?
Yes, more than once. I keep snapping at people over little things, and it’s really not like me.
During these blowups, have you ever become physically aggressive or damaged property?
I haven’t gotten physical or damaged anything. It’s been yelling and snapping at people, but even that scares me because it’s not how I usually am.
When you have these blowups, is it usually after you feel like someone might leave you or reject you?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it being about someone leaving me or rejecting me. It just feels like little things set me off.
Do these blowups tend to happen when something reminds you of the stressful event?

Yes. Anything connected to that day can set me off. I’ve been avoiding the house, the mortgage folder, even the herbs on my patio—just being near those things makes my chest tighten, and I can’t make myself go near them.
Do unwanted memories of that stressful event pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?
Yes. It just jumps into my head out of nowhere. I’ll be picking up a pan or opening a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m back there, smelling smoke and seeing the kitchen filling up before I can stop it.
During that event, did you think you might die or be seriously hurt?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know what I thought in that moment—I just remember everything happening so fast.
Was there a real fire during that event?
I… I’m not sure. I remember smoke and the kitchen filling up, but it was all so fast.
During that event, were you actually in danger of being seriously hurt or killed?
I honestly don’t know. I remember being scared and everything feeling chaotic, but I can’t tell you for sure whether I was actually in danger.
Did you see flames during that event?
I can’t say for sure. I remember the smoke, but I don’t clearly remember seeing flames.
Did anyone get seriously hurt in that event?
I don’t know. I can’t remember seeing anyone get seriously hurt.
Was there an explosion during that event?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember hearing or seeing an explosion.
Was anyone else in immediate danger of being seriously hurt or killed during that event?
I honestly don’t know. I can’t remember whether anyone else was in immediate danger.
Was the event a fire in your home?
I’m not sure. I can’t remember if it was in my home.
Were you injured during that event?
I... I’m not sure. I can’t remember whether I was injured.
